facts.text: DLP-printed AlCrFeNiSi green bodies were debound either in oxygen-rich ambient air or under continuous mechanical-pump evacuation that created an oxygen-deficient environment.
The debinding schedule included 1 h holds at 300 °C and 450 °C, followed by heating to 500 °C.
After debinding, specimens were solid-state sintered at 800, 1000, 1050, or 1100 °C for 24 h.
Printing used a 405 nm source at 19.57 mW/cm², a 100 s exposure, 70 μm layers, and 20 layers.
Oxygen-deficient debinding retained more carbon in former resin regions, reducing gas evolution and enabling lower porosity and stronger interparticle bonding.
During oxygen-rich debinding, rapidly escaping CO and CO2 caused pressure-driven surface cracking.
Particle-surface oxides formed under oxygen-rich conditions impeded interparticle mass transport and delayed densification.
Oxygen-deficient debinding eliminated the debinding-induced surface cracks observed after oxygen-rich debinding.
The printed layered morphology disappeared at 1050 °C after oxygen-deficient debinding, compared with 1100 °C after oxygen-rich debinding.
Oxygen-deficient debinding produced near-saturated consolidation and comparable maximum compressive strength at a sintering temperature 50 °C lower than the oxygen-rich baseline.
The oxygen-deficient specimen reached about 4.93 MPa at 1050 °C, whereas the oxygen-rich specimen required 1100 °C to reach 5.17 MPa.
After debinding, oxygen-deficient specimens contained 3.7 at.% oxygen and 33.6 at.% residual carbon, while oxygen-rich specimens contained 9.3 at.% oxygen and 21.7 at.% residual carbon.
